nodes.description: SMG9 is a core regulatory subunit of the heterotrimeric SMG1-SMG8-SMG9 phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase-related protein kinase (PIKK) complex that phosphorylates the RNA helicase UPF1 during mRNA surveillance. The p.(Val184Ala) G-domain defect is predicted to impair the recruitment or positioning of UPF1 on the SMG1-SMG8-SMG9 complex and modulate SMG1 serine/ threonine kinase activity without abolishing complex assembly. This node is marked provisional because direct biochemical assays of SMG1 kinase activity and UPF1 phosphorylation have not yet been performed on mutant p.(Val184Ala) patient cells.

nodes.description: The homozygous c.551T>C p.(Val184Ala) variant lies in exon 5 of SMG9 within the central nucleotide-binding G-domain of the SMG9 protein. Homology modeling using SWISS-MODEL predicts that substituting Val184 with Ala results in non-conservation of the coordinated magnesium ion and a structural defect in the G-domain ATP/GTP-binding pocket that faces the active kinase site of SMG1. nodes.description: Alongside quality control of premature termination codon (PTC)-bearing transcripts, the NMD machinery regulates normal endogenous physiological mRNAs (including transcripts with upstream open reading frames [uORFs] or long 3'UTRs). In whole-blood RNA-seq from homozygous p.(Val184Ala) patients, allele-specific expression analysis showed a functioning PTC-induced NMD mechanism, whereas differential gene expression analysis revealed 112 statistically significantly dysregulated genes with ~6.5 times more upregulated (97) than downregulated (15) genes. Prominent dysregulated genes include upregulated SMOX (logFC 2.1), OSBP2 (logFC 2.2), GPX3 (logFC 2.4), RAP1GAP (logFC 4.0), MAP1B (logFC 2.9), and HEY1 (logFC 2.0), as well as downregulated ZNF155 (logFC -2.3) and TUBB2A (logFC -2.9).

This analysis revealed genes whose expression is affected by dysfunctional SMG9, which are also candidates possibly contributing to the disease pathogenesis. The overall pattern observed was an increased expression of genes in the patient group compared to the control group, including ~ 6.5 times more upregulated (97) than downregulated (15) genes (p-value = 7.12e−16) (Supplementary Table 7), suggesting that dysfunctional SMG9 either affects NMD-regulated gene expression outside of the known canonical mechanisms or through a non-NMD regulatory mechanism.
